metadata.note: The Dakota Central Railway's lines in South Dakota, drawn as Chicago and North Western lines: the Dakota Central (chartered 1879) was a C&NW construction and land company whose property the C&NW operated from completion (ICC valuation), so there is no Dakota Central company or colour and no Rule 4 split. The 1907-1960 through route over the main line is the separate existing layer cnw_dakota_central_pierre.geojson; this layer draws the main line's pre-bridge era (to 1906) and the branches with a confirmed passenger year.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 edition - research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt
metadata.geometry_method: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles) plus OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) and OSM abandoned/rail-trail ways for lifted stretches, routed with opstrace.py: ways tagged old_railway_operator=C&NW (and RCP&E 'RCPE ... Subdivision' ways, which OSM tags old_railway_operator=CP after the DM&E's later owner) costed 1x, untagged rail 1.25x, cycleways 3x, any other named operator 12x; waypoints from the research report's via lists (Nominatim, each geocode's type checked; Clark SD returned the county and was hand-pinned), simplified Douglas-Peucker 8 m then trim_reversals.
metadata.colour: #E3B23C pulled programmatically from the existing C&NW feature in cnw_dakota_central_pierre.geojson (Rule 4); every 'Chicago and North Western Railway' feature in data/ checked identical.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] Brookings - Watertown: 1951 is the only confirmed year, both start and end open. [ANCHOR] Hawarden - Iroquois: 1884 only; 1951 is a candidate on unrecoverable Guide Table 59 times. Tracy - Huron 1879 and Huron - Pierre 1880 plausible, unconfirmed. Watertown - Redfield last-run date in 1950 not found; 1882-83 service unconfirmed. Branch passenger end dates for Huron - Oakes, Redfield - Gettysburg, Centerville - Yankton, Doland - Groton unknown. All headways and speeds (except the Brookings - Watertown mixed-train speed) are estimates. Construction-year conflicts ICC vs SD SHPO (Ordway-Columbia, Watertown-Redfield, Castlewood Jct-Watertown 1883 vs 1880, Iroquois-Hawarden, Centerville-Yankton) recorded in the research report, not resolved.
branches_deliberately_omitted: [2] Winona - Rapid City, 1907 on: already drawn as cnw_dakota_central_pierre.geojson (not edited here).
[4] Huron - Redfield - Aberdeen - Oakes (James River line): drawable NONE - no confirmed passenger year (Guide Table 59 fragments not attributable).
[6] Redfield - Gettysburg: drawable NONE - no confirmed passenger year (Guide Table 53 times not recoverable).
[8] Centerville - Yankton: drawable NONE - no confirmed passenger year; SHPO's 1935 Yankton - Mission Hill abandonment vs 1951 Guide unresolved.
[9] Doland - Groton: drawable NONE - freight-only by Sept 1951 and no passenger year confirmed at all (Rule 1).
[10] Gettysburg - Blunt: drawable NONE, and not Dakota Central (C&NW 1910).
[11] Tracy - Gary - Watertown: not a Dakota Central line (Winona and St. Peter land-grant line); belongs in a future C&NW / W&StP layer.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap rail geometry: 135.4 mi drawn against the documented Tracy 517.1 - Huron 653.4 = 136.3 mi (Official Guide Jan 1952 Table 67 mileage column / branchline SD 1). By tag: C&NW 133.8 mi, (untagged) 1.7 mi. No straight-line leg: every leg routed on OSM rail geometry (no leg longer than 1.6x its chord was ruled). Max waypoint offset from the line 0.8 km. LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEAT: the trace follows the track as it survives or is recorded in OSM today (live RCP&E or abandoned C&NW grade), not a survey of the original alignment; any line changes, yard rebuilds or station-approach relocations since the era drawn were not checked and may be drawn in their later form.

segments.note: Built by the Dakota Central Railway (chartered 1879; sold to the Winona and St. Peter Feb 1900, to the C&NW June 1900), which never ran a train of its own: the ICC valuation says its property was 'operated by the North Western ... from the completion of the line by sections', so the company and colour here are the C&NW's throughout. The Minnesota approach (Tracy - state line near Verdi) was the Chicago and Dakota Railway, likewise C&NW-operated from completion. Track reached Brookings 18 Oct 1879 and Huron by summer 1880. START 1880 is the first CONFIRMED passenger year: SD History 51:3 (2021) describes train traffic Tracy - Huron blockaded by the Hard Winter from Dec 1880 to early May 1881, so trains were running in autumn 1880; 1879 service east of Volga is plausible but unconfirmed. The winter blockade is a months-long gap, not a year gap, so it is not broken out. END 1906 IS NOT A SERVICE END: from 14 Oct 1907 this track is part of the through Winona - Rapid City feature (cnw-dakota-central-pierre), which draws 1907 on; this feature stops the year before so the two do not overlap. Headway (two trains a day each way) is an estimate and NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start 1880 from SD History 51:3 (Hard Winter blockade, Tracy - Huron) and SD SHPO chronology (Tracy - Volga 1879, Volga - Pierre 1880), as established in research/branches/dakota_central_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-25); end 1906 is the hand-off year to the existing 1907+ feature, not a passenger end. Headway and speed NOT sourced. Not re-checked during tracing.

By tag: C&NW 116.8 mi, (untagged) 1.5 mi. Every routed leg followed OSM rail geometry (no leg longer than 1.6x its chord was ruled); the one straight leg is the Huron yard join below. Max waypoint offset from the line 0.9 km. LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEAT: the trace follows the track as it survives or is recorded in OSM today (live RCP&E or abandoned C&NW grade), not a survey of the original alignment; any line changes, yard rebuilds or station-approach relocations since the era drawn were not checked and may be drawn in their later form. Blunt - Pierre needed two extra waypoints (Canning; a pinned point on the RCPE Pierre Subdivision east of Pierre at -100.192, 44.333) because the line swings about 18 km south of a straight Blunt - Pierre line, outside the router corridor round that chord; without them the router ruled a 20.7 mi straight line. STRAIGHT LEG: 0.7 mi (1.1 km) through the Huron yard, ruled from the end of the Tracy - Huron feature to the first traced node of this one (the two snapped to different yard nodes), so the two features join.

segments.note: Built by the Dakota Central Railway (chartered 1879; sold to the Winona and St. Peter Feb 1900, to the C&NW June 1900), which never ran a train of its own: the ICC valuation says its property was 'operated by the North Western ... from the completion of the line by sections', so the company and colour here are the C&NW's throughout. Track was completed to Pierre (east bank of the Missouri, a river terminus until the 1907 bridge) in 1880, but START 1881 is the first CONFIRMED passenger year: branchline.uk SD 1 tags the numbered sidings west of Huron ('Siding No. 1 ... No. 9') as 1881 Official Guide names; further 1883G names (Rex, Bramhall, Norbert) and an 1884G name at Harrold. Late-1880 service is plausible but unconfirmed, so this leg is split from Tracy - Huron rather than claiming 1880. END 1906 IS NOT A SERVICE END: from 14 Oct 1907 the line is part of the through Winona - Rapid City feature (cnw-dakota-central-pierre). Headway is an estimate and NOT sourced.

segments.note: Built by the Dakota Central Railway (chartered 1879; sold to the Winona and St. Peter Feb 1900, to the C&NW June 1900), which never ran a train of its own: the ICC valuation says its property was 'operated by the North Western ... from the completion of the line by sections', so the company and colour here are the C&NW's throughout. Built 1882 (ICC; SD SHPO has Watertown - Clark 1881, Clark - Redfield 1882). START 1884 is the first CONFIRMED passenger year (branchline.uk SD 2: 'Clark [Clark Centre q]' = 1884 Official Guide); the bracket is 1882 - 1884, earlier years not proven. END 1950: SD History 18:3 (1988), 'A Railroad Wins Friends' - early in 1950 the C&NW 'won regulatory approval to end passenger runs between Redfield and Tracy (a clanky motor train had plied these rails since the 1930s)'; runs existed when approval came, so 1950 is a service year, last-run date not found. Corroborated by the Sept 1951 Guide placing Table 128 'Watertown and Redfield' in the 'Freight Service only' block. The Redfield - Watertown - Tracy train (No. 106 in the 1930s-40s) ran on east over the Winona and St. Peter's Watertown - Gary - Tracy line, which is not drawn here. Freight continued; Watertown - Clark was abandoned in 1981 (SHPO) - an abandonment date, not a passenger one. Headway (one train a day) is an estimate and NOT sourced.

(Castlewood Junction / Sioux Valley Junction - Watertown, 1883 per ICC; 1880 per SD SHPO and abandonedrails - unresolved.) ANCHOR and OPEN: 1951 is the ONLY confirmed passenger year - Official Guide Table 44 'Brookings and Watertown', May 13, 1951, train 21 MIXED, lv Brookings 7:45, Bruce 8:45, Estelline 9:25, Dempster 9:40. Mixed-train service counts as passenger service (Rule 1). Service certainly ran earlier, but no earlier year is confirmed. 1951 is also the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when the mixed train stopped. Do not extend either way without evidence. The line was abandoned in 1993 (abandonedrails) - not a passenger date. Headway (one mixed train a day) is an estimate and NOT sourced.
